title: Dual Energy Focal Ablation of Premature Ventricular Complexes
official: Dual Energy (RF/PF) Focal Ablation of Premature Ventricular Complexes: the DUAL-PVC Prospective Clinical Trial
summary: The purpose of this research is to understand whether a dual-energy catheter ablation system that uses radiofrequency (RF) and pulsed-field (PF) energy can safely and effectively treat premature ventricular contractions (PVCs).

interventions.name: Dual Energy THERMOCOOL SMARTTOUCH™ SF (STSF) Bi-Directional Navigation catheter with TRUPULSE™ Generator

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* ≥10% burden of the target PVC on ambulatory rhythm monitoring within 3 months prior to enrollment. The qualifying ambulatory monitor may be of any duration (1-30 days) per standard of care and may be distinct from the baseline 12-lead Holter required within 30 days before ablation
* Guideline-supported indication for first-time or redo catheter ablation of PVCs at the judgment of the electrophysiologist. Specifically:

  * Patients with symptomatic PVCs for whom antiarrhythmic medications are ineffective, not tolerated, or not the patient's preference.
  * Suspected or confirmed PVC-induced cardiomyopathy
  * Enrollment of patients requiring a redo procedure will be capped at 30% of planned enrollment (n=18) if the target PVC is the same or similar to that targeted in previous procedure(s), per review of the study investigator
* Patients with and without known structural heart disease are eligible
* Ability to undergo study-directed cardiac MRI pre- and post-procedure
* Ability to undergo study-directed post-ablation coronary CT angiography
* Ability to provide written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* LVEF \<35%
* NYHA class IV
* Presence of multifocal PVCs (\>=3 distinct morphologies) on available pre-baseline standard-of-care ambulatory monitor and ECG tracings per the review of the study team.
* PVCs attributable to a reversible or non-cardiac cause (e.g., electrolyte imbalance or active thyroid disease).
* History of sustained VT or VF.
* Current or recent (\<4 weeks) decompensated heart failure.
* Active systemic infection.
* Contraindication to LGE-MRI or contrast CT.
* Known allergy to iodinated contrast dye that cannot be adequately managed with pre-medication protocol.
* Thrombocytopenia (platelet count \<50,000/mm³) or known coagulopathy.
* Contraindication to systemic anticoagulation.
* Severe valvular disease requiring future intervention.
* Mechanical valve prosthesis.
* Pregnancy.
* Recent acute coronary syndrome (\<6 months).
* Un-revascularized coronary artery disease.
* Presence of left ventricular assist device (LVAD) or transplanted heart.
* Presence of intracardiac thrombus.
* Current use of inotropes.
* Recent stroke or TIA (\<6 months).
* Presence of a systemic illness likely to limit survival to \<1 year.
* Patient enrollment in other clinical study that could conflict with the current investigation.
